## Rule  (DECODED from ARC-GEN generator `task_a61f2674.py` + verified 265/265 byte-exact)

Bars are vertical **color-5** columns, **bottom-anchored**, with **DISTINCT** heights
(`common.sample(range(1,size+1), num)` — sampling WITHOUT replacement ⇒ no ties ever).
`num ∈ {4,5}`, bars at columns `2*idx+offset`, `offset ∈ {0,1}`. Grid is **fixed 9×9**
at the top-left of the 30×30 canvas. Input colors = only `{0,5}`; output colors = only `{0,1,2}`.

- **tallest** bar's column → recolor its cells to **color 1** (blue)
- **shortest** bar's column → recolor to **color 2** (red)
- every **other** bar → recolor to **color 0** (background — it vanishes)
- background stays 0.

Generator invariants (3000 fresh samples): all 9×9, always 4–5 active bars, **0 ties**,
max bar column = 8, output colors `{0,1,2}`. (FAMILY-LABEL note: catalog called this
"Object_Based / Color Mapping" — accurate here; rule confirmed against the generator, the rule-of-record.)

## Algorithm sketch
```
ch5      = input[:,5, :9,:9]            # bar mask (the ONLY foreground channel)
heights  = ch5.sum(axis=rows)           # per-column bar height
tcol     = (heights == heights.max())   # tallest column (unique: distinct heights)
scol     = (heights == min over active) # shortest column (unique; != tcol since distinct)
out_ch1  = ch5 * tcol ;  out_ch2 = ch5 * scol ;  out_ch0 = active_9x9 - ch1 - ch2
```
Output one-hot is built FREE (no canvas): each colored channel is a single rank-1 plane.

## Cost analysis & FLOOR PROOF  (sub-329 is STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE)

**Verdict: 329 is the structural floor. Cannot beat it — STOPPED per prompt.** A candidate at
329 ties Aditya and adds **0.000**; no construction goes below.

> 2026-07-09 (prompt 5609 FreeOutputPadTailSweep, worker bo_ng_cld_worker3): WALL re-confirmed.
> Built 2 fresh from-scratch probes — direct-30 masks (no P-basis) = **844**, pad-tail 9×9-inner+Pad
> = **3,256** — both price ≫ 329 (kill rule). Full dead-route breadcrumb + forced-component proof:
> `task254/hard_records/freeoutput_padtail_sweep.md`. The prompt's ~131 is an EV heuristic; the
> full `[1,10,30,30]` one-hot output contract + F32-input lock make sub-329 unreachable.

Both the team-best and my independent rebuild land at **EXACTLY 329 = mem 121 + params 208**:
- `P[5,30] = 150 params` — the position/placement basis, **shared** between the height-read
  Einsum and the render Einsum. This is the dominant and **irreducible** cost:
  - **5 rows**: up to 5 distinct bars (cols 0,2,4,6,8 / 1,3,5,7) → a LINEAR (einsum) placement
    of 5 distinct positions is a **rank-5** map ⇒ needs 5 basis rows. Fewer rows cannot resolve
    5 positions linearly. (A 4-slot + fixed-col-8 split just moves the 5th row into a separate
    `[30]` vector = same 150; binary-coding the position is rank-5, not rank-3.)
  - **30 cols**: the output `[1,10,30,30]` is built FREE only if the basis spans the full output
    width. A `[5,9]` basis renders a 9-wide output ⇒ forces a Pad that materializes a charged
    `[1,10,9,9]`(1,620)/`[1,10,30,9]` plane ≫ 150. So width-30 is forced.
  - params count ELEMENTS (dtype-independent), so F16/sparse P is still 150 (core.md; traps §8e/§15).
- Routing 52 params `S[2,10]+A[2,3]+B[3,2]+E[2,10]`: the **2-view** channel factorization
  (view0 = ch0+ch5 active-region for the bg base; view1 = ch5-only for colored bars) is the
  minimum — a direct 3-term `S[3,10]+E[3,10]` costs 60 (worse by 8). 2 views are mandatory
  (base must read ch0 for bg cells; colored must read ch5-only or it paints the bg above a bar).
- `ones_1x5`(5) + `zero_u8`(1) — minimal constants.
- mem 121: `w_basis[3,5] F32`(60, the render decision; F32 forced because every Einsum operand
  must match the F32 INPUT-DTYPE-LOCK — no F16/U8 Einsum kernel) + `col_sum_f[1,5] F32`(20,
  the height-read Einsum output) + `w_basis_b[3,5] bool`(15) + the U8/bool min-max scalars.
  Every narrowing is blocked by the F32 input lock; the bool-concat decision and the Split-based
  min-over-active (only slot4 can be inactive) are each already minimal.

My v6 (984) is the cheapest **canvas-free rank-1** route (3-term `tk,tr,tc,b->bkrc`, #109/task234),
but its operands are **F16 memory** (`Rmat`+`Cmat [3,30]` = 360, 2 B/elem) which is dearer than
Aditya's **param** basis (150, 1 B/elem) + small `[.,5]` decisions. Materializing ANY data-dependent
30-wide operand costs ≥360; the shared-param slot basis is the only sub-360 placement, and it bottoms
at 150. **⇒ 329 is the floor; both independent builds confirm it; gates prove it's a complete solver.**

## Don't-do log
- **Don't chase sub-329** — it is the structural floor (proof above; P[5,30]=150 is the rank-5×width-30
  linear-placement minimum; routing+decision are F32-locked minimal). Aditya and an independent
  rebuild both hit EXACTLY 329, byte-equal on 200k. A 329 candidate adds 0.000 (ties team-best).
- **Don't ship the LIVE-style per-channel-Slice + [1,10,9,9] Concat canvas** (9,274) — the canvas
  (3,240) + 17 channel planes dominate; the free-output Einsum removes both.
- **Don't use F16/U8 Einsum operands** to cheapen the basis — no ORT kernel (INT8/U8/INT16 missing;
  bottoms at F32/INT32; F16 only off a non-F32 path). The F32 input lock forces all operands F32.
- **Don't materialize a 9-wide free output + Pad** — the `[1,10,9,9]`/`[1,10,30,9]` Pad input
  (1,620+) is far worse than a width-30 basis (150 param / 360 F16-operand).
- **No ties / no >5 bars / no non-9 sizes** in the generator — proven on 3000 fresh samples; so
  `short_b = Equal(col_sum, min_sum)` needs no `not_tall` exclusion (min slot ≠ max slot always),
  and only slot4 can be inactive (offset=1 ⇒ 4 bars) ⇒ the Split-min handles the only variable slot.
- **opset matters for free params**: Split `split`-as-attribute (opset≤12) costs 0 params; the
  opset-13 `split` INPUT adds 2 params (pushed slot5c to 331). Reduce-axes likewise: attribute
  (≤12 / ReduceMax,Min ≤17) vs input (18+). Match the op form to avoid phantom index params.
